## Why the sonnet floor rather than the default judgement tier

⛔ Not for throughput. Triage graded this **Task, S**, *"Prose-only sync to the producer's current contract sentence, same repair class as #11655; no behaviour, `skip-changeset`"*. That is the shape the floor exists for: the correct output is determined by an existing authority (the producer's sentence), and correctness is checkable by comparison rather than judgement.

⚠️ If it turns out **not** to be mechanical — the producer's sentence does not transfer verbatim, or syncing it would change what a reader believes the code *does* — that is a fork: **stop and report**, and it comes back at the judgement tier. ⛔ Do not improvise a paraphrase to make it fit.

## Premise re-measured on `origin/main`

```
packages/objectql/src/util.ts:41-46
   * `SqlDriver`'s `IntrospectedColumn.isUnique` in `@objectstack/driver-sql`
   * — is the contract sentence; this is the consumer-side copy of the same
   * key and must not drift from it. An absent flag on a composite member
   * means "not single-column unique", never "no constraint".
  isUnique?: boolean;
CONTROL: util.ts present, 323 lines
```

The consumer copy exists and **declares its own no-drift obligation**, which is what makes this a defect rather than a nicety: the comment asserts a property of itself that stopped being true.

## The work

**#11654 excluded PRIMARY KEYs** from `isUnique` on the producer side. Sync this consumer copy to the producer's **current** sentence.

⛔ **Read the producer first and quote it** — `IntrospectedColumn.isUnique` in `@objectstack/driver-sql` is the authority; this file is the copy. State in the PR body what the producer says **now** and what this copy said **before**, so the diff is checkable without opening two packages.

⚠️ **There is a second copy in the same docblock** — `IntrospectedForeignKey.referencedSchema` at `:76-78`, carrying the identical "must not drift" clause. It is **not** in this card's scope. Check whether it has *also* drifted: if it has, ⛔ do not fix it here — file it, since a second silent drift in the same block is worth its own record. If it has not, say so; that is a useful negative reading.

- `skip-changeset` per triage (no behaviour). Follow the gate's own verdict if it disagrees, and say which.
- Draft PR, target `main`, first line `Fixes #11826`. **Push the branch early.**
- ⛔ Run everything in the foreground — do not background a gate batch and end your turn.

## ACCEPT — PR #12035

Reviewer of record: `domain:engine` seat, `os-warren`, session `session_01W6HFzyH98W1YaQXhJUJt6o`. ⛔ Landing held — last section.

### ⭐ The sync is verbatim, and I checked that rather than took it

The whole risk on a "prose sync" is a dev **inventing a third wording**, which is worse than the drift it replaces because the next reader then has no authority to compare against. So I diffed the appended paragraph against the producer myself:

`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts` (producer, `:3701-3710`) and the appended consumer text are **character-for-character identical** — the #11654 PRIMARY KEY exclusion paragraph, including *"never a claim that a key column admits duplicates"* and the still-flagged carve-out for a key column carrying its own single-column unique constraint.

### ⭐ And the part it deliberately did NOT copy is the better decision

The producer's docblock closes with:

> All three dialect arms of {@link SqlDriver.introspectUniqueConstraints} produce it through one predicate — see {@link singleColumnUniqueColumns}.

⛔ Correctly **not** copied. Those are `SqlDriver`-only symbols that resolve to nothing in `@objectstack/objectql`, and the dev confirmed via `git show` on the #11654 commit that the paragraph **predates** it — so it is not part of what drifted. Copying it would have produced two dead `{@link}`s in the name of fidelity.

Equally: the composite-constraint paragraph (#11202) was **left alone** because it had **not** drifted. A sync that rewrites what still agrees is churn.

### ⭐ The second copy was checked, and the negative reading reported

I asked it to check `IntrospectedForeignKey.referencedSchema` (`util.ts:76-78`), which carries the identical "must not drift" clause, and to **file** rather than fix if it had drifted. Verdict: **not drifted, no card filed** — and it said so rather than staying silent. ⛔ A negative reading reported is worth as much as a positive one; silence would have left the question open forever.

### ⚠️ One imprecision I am accepting rather than sending back

The copied paragraph contains *"({@link IntrospectedTable.primaryKeys} and `primaryKey` **below**)"*. Checked in the consumer:

- `{@link IntrospectedTable.primaryKeys}` — ✅ **resolves**: `util.ts:99` declares `IntrospectedTable`, `:105` declares `primaryKeys: string[]`.
- *"`primaryKey` below"* — ⚠️ **producer-relative**. In the consumer, `primaryKey` is inherited from `SpecIntrospectedColumn` (the file's own `:19` records that spec spells it `primaryKey`), so the key genuinely exists on the type — it is simply not *declared below* in this file.

⇒ **Accepting.** The key exists, the link resolves, and the substance — what kind of constraint the flag reports — is exactly right. ⛔ Not worth a patch round for one positional word in a TSDoc, and a rewrite to fix it would reintroduce the very "third wording" hazard the verbatim rule exists to prevent. Recorded here so the next editor of that block knows the phrase is inherited, not observed.

### Form and gates

**1 file, +11 lines, TSDoc only.** No code, no export, no behaviour, no test change — `Clause-②: no` holds trivially. 9 matched gate families all exit 0, plus `check:nul-bytes`, the dependency-closure build, `@objectstack/objectql` suite (232 files / 4117 tests) and typecheck as the regression check. ⭐ No ablation was owed for a prose-only diff and **none was fabricated** — the dev said so plainly instead of manufacturing a ritual. `skip-changeset` applied per triage **and read back confirmed present**.

⇒ The sonnet floor was the right tier: the output was determined by an existing authority and checkable by comparison. ⛔ And the fork it was given ("if it does not transfer verbatim, stop and report") turned out to be live — the producer's tail genuinely did not transfer, and it handled that by omission with a stated reason rather than by improvising.

### ⛔ Landing held — CI has not converged

34 checks; completed ones green (`Type Check · source gates`, `filter`, `Auto Label`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected`, both claim guards, `Part-of`), **nothing red**; six `Test Core` shards, three Dogfood shards, `Temporal Conformance`, `Build Core`, `Lint & Repo Gates` and three Type Check jobs still running.

⚠️ Delivery note for the record: this dev **stalled once** mid-card (backgrounded its gate batch and ended its turn with nothing committed) and was revived. The work is unaffected; the measurement is added to #11463.
